title: Section 121 — Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to deter public servant from his duty

content.overview: BNS s. 121 — Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to deter public servant from his duty.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to deter public servant from his duty. BNS restatement of IPC 332 / 333. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 332 / 333. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 121 is the rule on “Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to deter public servant from his duty”. The section provides that (1) Whoever voluntarily causes hurt to any person being a public servant in the discharge of his duty as such public servant, or with intent to prevent or deter that person or any other public servant from discharging his duty as such public servant or in consequence of anything done or attempted to be done by that person in the lawful discharge of his duty as such public servant, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine, or with both. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 121 exists so that “Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to deter public servant from his duty” has a closed legal test in Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Homicide, organised crime, terrorism, hurt, acid, restraint, assault, kidnapping and trafficking.

The provision in detail
121. (1) Whoever voluntarily causes hurt to any person being a public servant in the discharge of his duty as such public servant, or with intent to prevent or deter that person or any other public servant from discharging his duty as such public servant or in consequence of anything done or attempted to be done by that person in the lawful discharge of his duty as such public servant, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine, or with both

(2) Whoever voluntarily causes grievous hurt to any person being a public servant in the discharge of his duty as such public servant, or with intent to prevent or deter that person or any other public servant from discharging his duty as such public servant or in consequence of anything done or attempted to be done by that person in the lawful discharge of his duty as such public servant, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine

learningObjectives: Master the aggravated offences protecting public servants under BNS s. 121.
Analyze the statutory criteria: victim is a public servant acting in the discharge of official duties, or attacked to deter/prevent discharge of duty.
Contrast sub-section (1) (hurt: up to 5 years and fine) with sub-section (2) (grievous hurt: up to 10 years and fine).
Understand the consolidation of IPC ss. 332 and 333.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 121 consolidates provisions protecting public servants from violent obstruction: sub-section (1) punishes voluntarily causing hurt to any person being a public servant in the discharge of his duty as such, or with intent to prevent or deter that person or any other public servant from discharging his duty, or in consequence of anything done in lawful discharge of duty, with imprisonment up to five years, fine, or both; sub-section (2) punishes voluntarily causing grievous hurt for any such reason with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and fine.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Safeguards public administration and the rule of law by penalizing physical violence directed against public officers engaged in lawful duty.
statutoryFramework: Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body, BNS s. 121 (consolidating IPC ss. 332 and 333).
Sub-section (1): Voluntarily causing hurt to deter public servant — imprisonment of either description up to five years, or fine, or both (increased from 3 years under IPC 332).
Sub-section (2): Voluntarily causing grievous hurt to deter public servant — imprisonment of either description up to ten years, and fine.
Contexts of liability: (1) While public servant is in discharge of duty; (2) With intent to prevent/deter discharge of duty; (3) In consequence of lawful past acts.
essentialIngredients: The victim was a public servant.
The accused voluntarily caused hurt (sub-section 1) OR grievous hurt (sub-section 2) to the public servant.
The hurt was caused while the public servant was discharging his official duty; OR
With the intent to prevent or deter the public servant from discharging his duty; OR
In consequence of something done or attempted by the public servant in lawful discharge of his duty.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 121 consolidates former IPC 332 and 333, providing heightened penal protection to public servants (such as police officers, tax inspectors, doctors in public hospitals, or municipal demolition squads) who face physical violence while discharging lawful public duties. To attract Section 121, the public servant must have been acting in lawful discharge of their official functions, or attacked with the specific intent to deter them from acting, or attacked in retaliation for past official acts. In BNS 2023, the legislature increased the general maximum penalty under sub-section (1) from three years to five years imprisonment, reflecting increased deterrence against assaults on public servants, while sub-section (2) punishes grievous hurt with up to ten years imprisonment and fine.
examples: Teaching example (Assault on traffic police officer): A motorist stopped for running a red light punches the traffic constable in the face and twists his arm to prevent the constable from issuing a challan. The motorist is liable under s. 121(1) (up to five years).

Teaching example (Grievous hurt to demolition squad): An illegal encroacher strikes a municipal engineer on the head with an iron crowbar, fracturing his skull, to halt a court-ordered demolition drive. The encroacher is liable under s. 121(2) (up to ten years and fine).
distinctions: Section 121 vs Section 115: Section 115 applies to hurt against private citizens (up to 1 year); Section 121 applies when the victim is a public servant on duty (up to 5 years for hurt, up to 10 years for grievous hurt).

Section 121 vs Section 132 (Criminal Force against Public Servant): Section 132 penalizes assault or criminal force without bodily hurt (up to 2 years); Section 121 requires proof of actual hurt or grievous hurt.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether an accused who attacked an electricity department meter reader with a stick, fracturing the reader's wrist while the reader was disconnecting an illegal power line, is liable under s. 121.
Rule: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt to a public servant in the discharge of official duty constitutes an offence under BNS s. 121(2).
Application: The meter reader is a public servant discharging lawful duty, and the wrist fracture constitutes grievous hurt under s. 116(g).
Conclusion: The accused is guilty under BNS s. 121(2) and faces up to ten years imprisonment.
